_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

The `bibliography` front matter field is a **filename only**. The `distill` layout prepends `/assets/bibliography/` when building the page:

```99:99:_layouts/distill.html
      <d-bibliography src="{{ page.bibliography | prepend: '/assets/bibliography/' | relative_url }}"></d-bibliography>
```

So for your post, it resolves to:

**`assets/bibliography/dynamic-decoding.bib`**

That file is shared with the draft `_drafts/2023-12-25-dynamic-decoding.md`, which uses the same `bibliography: dynamic-decoding.bib` setting.

This is separate from the Jekyll Scholar setup in `_config.yml`, which uses `_bibliography/` (e.g. `mine.bib`, `papers.bib`) for the publications page and other `{% bibliography %}` tags. Distill posts load their `.bib` from `assets/bibliography/` via the `<d-bibliography>` web component at build/render time.

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

Yes — the TOC is implemented, but only as a **manual** front-matter list in the distill layout. The `jekyll-toc` note in the comments is **not** implemented.

In `_layouts/distill.html`, if `page.toc` is set, it renders a "Contents" nav with links built from each entry's `name`:

```73:89:_layouts/distill.html
        {% if page.toc -%}
        <d-contents>
          <nav class="l-text figcaption">
          <h3>Contents</h3>
            {% for section in page.toc -%}
            <div><a href="#{{ section.name | slugify }}">{{ section.name }}</a></div>
            {% if section.subsections -%}
            <ul>
              {% for subsection in section.subsections -%}
              <li><a href="#{{ subsection.name | slugify }}">{{ subsection.name }}</a></li>
              {% endfor %}
            </ul>
            {%- endif -%}
            {%- endfor %}
          </nav>
        </d-contents>
        {%- endif %}
```

How it works:

1. You list sections under `toc:` in front matter (each with a `name:`).
2. The layout slugifies each name and links to `#that-slug`.
3. Those links only work if your markdown headings match exactly (e.g. `# Introduction` → anchor `#introduction`).
4. You can optionally nest entries with `subsections:`.

What is **not** implemented: auto-generating the TOC from headings via `jekyll-toc`. You maintain the list by hand.

For your CTMC post specifically, the TOC block looks copied from the dynamic-decoding draft — `"Ove"` looks truncated, and `"What are Belief Functions?"` doesn't fit a CTMC post. The post body is also empty right now, so even with the layout support, the TOC wouldn't link anywhere useful yet.

Upstream [al-folio](https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio) has auto TOC, but **not for distill posts**. It depends on the layout.

### Distill posts — still manual (same as your fork)

The upstream example distill post (`_posts/2018-12-22-distill.md`) uses the same manual `toc:` list and the same “we may want to automate… using jekyll-toc” comment. There is no auto-generation from headings for `layout: distill`.

So for your CTMC post, upstream would work the same way: you hand-maintain section names under `toc:`.

### Regular posts — auto TOC is implemented

Upstream ships `jekyll-toc` and documents two auto modes:

1. **Top of post** — set `toc: beginning: true`  
   Example: [`_posts/2023-03-20-table-of-contents.md`](https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio/blob/main/_posts/2023-03-20-table-of-contents.md)

2. **Sidebar** — set `toc: sidebar: left` (or `right`)  
   Example: [`_posts/2023-04-25-sidebar-table-of-contents.md`](https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio/blob/main/_posts/2023-04-25-sidebar-table-of-contents.md)

On current upstream `main` (v1.x), the sidebar uses **Tocbot** instead of the older bootstrap-toc your fork still has.

### Summary

| Layout | Auto TOC in upstream? |
|--------|------------------------|
| `post` with `toc: beginning: true` | Yes (`jekyll-toc`) |
| `post` with `toc: sidebar: left/right` | Yes (Tocbot in v1.x) |
| `distill` with `toc: - name: ...` | No — manual only |

The `jekyll-toc` note in your distill front matter is a future idea upstream never implemented for distill either. If you want auto TOC for the CTMC post without maintaining the list by hand, you’d either switch to `layout: post` with `toc: sidebar: left`, or wire `jekyll-toc` into the distill layout yourself.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
d-contents is merely an al-folio CSS and layout wrapper. It is not a Distill web component from template.v2.js.

The native Distill auto-TOC is `<d-toc>`, which scans h2 and h3 headings. Replacing the manual loop with `<d-toc></d-toc>` inside `d-contents` is very easy—only a few lines in `distill.html`. However, `d-toc` only captures h2 and h3, runs client-side on window.onload, and may clash with `d-contents` CSS. Kramdown must generate heading IDs for this to work. Using `{% toc %}` inside the `d-contents` nav is another option.

jekyll-toc is already installed. The current `page.toc` key holds an array of section objects, but jekyll-toc expects a boolean or object shape. These two structures conflict. jekyll-toc also emits nested `<ul>` elements, while `d-contents` CSS targets `<div>` children, so the two approaches do not match.

jekyll-toc is not especially easy to wire into the distill layout. Its semantic meaning conflicts with the existing `page.toc` field, and its HTML structure clashes with `d-contents` CSS. The native `<d-toc>` element remains the simpler choice.

Liquid evaluates `page.toc` as truthy even when it is an array, so the existing layout conditional would still trigger jekyll-toc. The `{% toc %}` tag generates the list internally from the page content, ignoring the front matter shape. This makes `{% toc %}` a viable replacement for the manual loop without changing the `page.toc` data structure.

Kramdown attributes such as `{:toc}` and `{::options}` only work inside markdown files, not in Liquid layouts. The `{% toc %}` tag from the jekyll-toc plugin is the correct way to generate the table of contents within a layout. Level filtering for jekyll-toc must be configured in `_config.yml` instead of inline.
</details></think>

**Partly easy, but jekyll-toc is an awkward fit for distill.** A small layout change can wire it up, but you’ll likely need CSS tweaks and anchor alignment. There’s also a simpler option already in your distill JS.

### What you have now

Distill uses a **manual** `<d-contents>` sidebar: front-matter names are slugified into `#anchors`. That’s why the comment mentions jekyll-toc as a future idea — it was never wired in your fork (or upstream’s distill example).

### Wiring jekyll-toc

`jekyll-toc` is already installed. A minimal change in `_layouts/distill.html` would look like:

```liquid
{% if page.toc == true %}
<d-contents>
  <nav class="l-text figcaption">
    <h3>Contents</h3>
    {% toc %}
  </nav>
  <toc-line></toc-line>
</d-contents>
{% elsif page.toc %}
  {# existing manual loop #}
{% endif %}

{{ content | inject_anchors }}
```

That’s only ~10 lines, but the friction is elsewhere:

1. **Front matter API** — Today `toc:` is a list (`- name: ...`). Auto mode would need a different shape, e.g. `toc: true` vs `toc: beginning: true` on regular posts. You’d need a clear convention.
2. **HTML mismatch** — `d-contents` CSS expects top-level `<div><a>…</a></div>`. jekyll-toc emits nested `<ul class="section-nav">`. Links will work, but styling will look off until you adjust `_sass/_distill.scss` or jekyll-toc’s `list_class` in `_config.yml`.
3. **Heading levels** — jekyll-toc defaults to h1–h6 unless configured. Distill’s native TOC only scans **h2/h3**. You’d want something like `min_level: 2, max_level: 3` in `_config.yml`.
4. **Anchor IDs** — Manual TOC uses Jekyll’s `slugify`; jekyll-toc and kramdown may generate different IDs. Using `inject_anchors` on `{{ content }}` keeps TOC links and heading IDs in sync.
5. **`{% toc %}` scope** — It works for `_posts`, which is fine for your CTMC post.

So: **doable in one sitting**, but not drop-in.

### Easier option: `<d-toc>` (already bundled)

Distill’s JS already auto-builds a TOC from **h2/h3** at runtime:

```javascript
const headings = article.querySelectorAll('h2, h3');
```

You could replace the manual loop with:

```liquid
{% if page.toc %}
<d-contents>
  <d-toc></d-toc>
  <toc-line></toc-line>
</d-contents>
{% endif %}
```

Then set `toc: true` (or any truthy flag) and write sections as `##` / `###` — no front-matter section list, no jekyll-toc config.

Tradeoffs:
- Client-side (runs on `window.onload`), not build-time
- Renders its own “Table of contents” heading and markup, so you may still want CSS tweaks inside `d-contents`
- Ignores `#` (h1) headings

### Recommendation

| Approach | Effort | Best when |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Keep manual `toc:` list | None | Few sections, custom labels |
| `<d-toc>` | Very low (~5 lines) | Auto from `##`/`###`, distill-native |
| jekyll-toc | Medium | You want build-time TOC and same plugin as regular posts |

For a CTMC distill post, **`<d-toc>` is the path of least resistance**. jekyll-toc is reasonable if you specifically want build-time generation and consistency with `layout: post`, but expect a short CSS + config pass.

If you want, I can wire up either `<d-toc>` or jekyll-toc in `_layouts/distill.html` and add the matching `_config.yml` / SCSS tweaks.

$(document).ready(function() {
    // Populate distill sidebar TOC. d-toc uses window.onload, which other
    // scripts can overwrite; run this explicitly after the page loads.
    function populateDistillTOC() {
        const article = document.querySelector("d-article");
        const toc = document.querySelector("d-toc");
        if (!article || !toc || toc.getAttribute("prerendered") === "true") {
            return;
        }

        const headings = article.querySelectorAll("h1, h2, h3");
        let html = '<nav role="navigation" class="table-of-contents"></nav><h3>Contents</h3><ul>';
        let hasEntries = false;

        for (const el of headings) {
            const isInTitle = el.closest("d-title") !== null;
            const isException = el.hasAttribute("no-toc");
            if (isInTitle || isException || !el.getAttribute("id")) {
                continue;
            }

            hasEntries = true;
            const title = el.textContent;
            const link = "#" + el.getAttribute("id");
            let line = '<li><a href="' + link + '">' + title + "</a></li>";
            if (el.tagName === "H3") {
                line = "<ul>" + line + "</ul>";
            } else {
                line += "<br>";
            }
            html += line;
        }

        html += "</ul>";
        if (!hasEntries) {
            return;
        }

        toc.innerHTML = html;
        toc.setAttribute("prerendered", "true");
    }

    window.addEventListener("load", populateDistillTOC);
    if (document.readyState === "complete") {
        populateDistillTOC();

The root cause was **`enable_progressbar: true`**. The progress bar script in `_includes/scripts/progressBar.html` was doing:

```javascript
window.onload = function () { ... }
```

That **replaced** the handler `d-toc` registered the same way, so the TOC never populated.

### Fixes applied

1. **`progressBar.html`** — switched to `window.addEventListener("load", ...)` so it no longer clobbers other load handlers.
2. **`overrides.js`** — added a reliable `populateDistillTOC()` that runs on `load` and fills `<d-toc>` from `#` / `##` / `###` headings.

Hard refresh the page (`Cmd+Shift+R`). You should see a sidebar with **Overview** and **Poisson Processes**.

On viewports under 1024px wide, the TOC moves above the article body instead of sitting in a left sidebar — widen the window if you're checking on a narrow panel.

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

Yes, you have **MathJax enabled**, but **no custom preamble** (no macro definitions or extra TeX packages beyond the default).

Config lives in `_includes/scripts/mathjax.html`:

```4:8:_includes/scripts/mathjax.html
    window.MathJax = {
      tex: {
        tags: 'ams'
      }
    };
```

That’s included when `enable_math: true` in `_config.yml` (currently set). MathJax version is **3.2.0** (`_config.yml` → `mathjax.version`).

So right now you only get:
- AMS-style equation numbering (`tags: 'ams'`)
- Default MathJax TeX packages/macros

There is **no** `macros: { ... }`, `packages: [...]`, or `\newcommand`-style preamble block.

**Note for distill posts:** `layout: distill` loads MathJax *and* uses **KaTeX** via the Distill template (`$...$`, `$$...$$` in `distill.html`). Custom MathJax macros in `mathjax.html` won’t apply to KaTeX-rendered math in distill posts unless you configure KaTeX separately.

To add a MathJax preamble, extend `_includes/scripts/mathjax.html`, e.g.:

```javascript
window.MathJax = {
  tex: {
    tags: 'ams',
    macros: {
      R: '\\mathbb{R}',
      E: '\\mathbb{E}',
    }
  }
};
```

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

**Partially.** KaTeX has no LaTeX-style `\documentclass` preamble string like MathJax can use. Instead it supports **macros** and **in-math `\newcommand` definitions**.

### What KaTeX supports

1. **`macros` option** — pass custom commands when rendering:
   ```javascript
   katex.render("x \in \R", element, {
     macros: {
       "\\R": "\\mathbb{R}",
       "\\E": "\\mathbb{E}[#1]",
     }
   });
   ```

2. **Preamble-style setup** — run definitions once with a shared `macros` object:
   ```javascript
   const macros = {};
   katex.renderToString(
     "\\newcommand{\\R}{\\mathbb{R}}",
     { macros, globalGroup: true }
   );
   // then render all math with the same `macros` object
   renderMathInElement(document.body, { macros });
   ```

3. **In-content definitions** — `\newcommand`, `\def`, `\gdef`, etc. work inside math, but `\gdef`/`\global\def` only persist if you reuse the same `macros` object across renders.

There is **no** built-in `preamble: "..."` config option (that’s been requested but not added).

### On your site

Distill posts use KaTeX via the Distill template. Your `_layouts/distill.html` only configures delimiters:

```40:53:_layouts/distill.html
      "katex": {
        "delimiters": [
          {
            "left": "$",
            "right": "$",
            "display": false
          },
          {
            "left": "$$",
            "right": "$$",
            "display": true
          }
        ]
      }
```

No `macros` are set, and `DMath.katexOptions` is passed straight through to `katex.render()` / `renderMathInElement()`. So **you don’t have a KaTeX preamble configured today**.

### Practical options for your CTMC post

| Approach | Works in distill? |
|----------|------------------|
| Add `"macros": { "\\R": "\\mathbb{R}" }` to the `katex` block in front matter / layout | Yes (if Distill passes it through — it should via `DMath.katexOptions`) |
| Define per-post in `_layouts/distill.html` or `overrides.js` | Yes |
| Use `\newcommand` inline in each equation | Yes, but verbose |
| MathJax `macros` in `mathjax.html` | No for distill math (that uses KaTeX) |

**Bottom line:** KaTeX supports macro preambles via the `macros` option (or a one-time `globalGroup` setup), not a raw LaTeX preamble string. Your site doesn’t use that yet for distill posts.

If you want, I can add a shared `macros` block to your distill layout for common CTMC notation (`\R`, `\E`, `\Prob`, etc.).

**Not out of the box.** Your site has no per-post `preamble.tex` support today. Distill posts use **KaTeX**, regular posts use **MathJax**, and neither is wired to read a `.tex` file automatically.

### What you have now

| Post type | Math engine | Preamble support |
|-----------|-------------|------------------|
| `layout: distill` (e.g. CTMC) | KaTeX | Delimiters only in `_layouts/distill.html` |
| `layout: post` | MathJax | `tags: 'ams'` only in `_includes/scripts/mathjax.html` |

Distill passes front-matter `katex` config into `DMath.katexOptions`, so you *could* add a `"macros": { ... }` object per post in JSON — but that's not a `.tex` file, and nothing reads one today.

### Can a `preamble.tex` work per post?

**Partially**, with custom wiring. Important limits:

1. **KaTeX ≠ LaTeX** — a full `\documentclass` / `\usepackage{...}` preamble won't work. Only macro-style content is usable, e.g.:
   ```tex
   \newcommand{\R}{\mathbb{R}}
   \newcommand{\E}[1]{\mathbb{E}\left[#1\right]}
   ```

2. **KaTeX has no `preamble:` option** — you load definitions by either:
   - passing a `macros` object to `renderMathInElement`, or
   - running the `.tex` contents once with `{ macros, globalGroup: true }` before rendering the page.

3. **MathJax** — similarly, you'd inject the file contents into `window.MathJax.tex.macros` at build time; no native `\input{preamble.tex}`.

### Practical patterns (closest to what you want)

**A. Per-post `.tex` file + front matter** (needs a small custom hook)

```yaml
# _posts/2026-05-10-ctmc.md
preamble: ctmc.tex
```

Store `assets/tex/preambles/ctmc.tex`, then at build time:
- Jekyll reads the file
- Injects it into the distill `katex` config or a `<script type="text/tex-preamble">` tag
- `overrides.js` runs KaTeX on that string before auto-rendering `$...$` math

**B. Per-post macros in front matter** (works now, no `.tex` file)

You'd need to extend `distill.html` to merge post-specific katex options — currently the layout hardcodes delimiters and ignores per-post overrides.

**C. Inline in the post** (works now, no setup)

Put definitions in a hidden/math block at the top of the markdown; KaTeX can process `\newcommand` with `globalGroup`. Verbose and not ideal for reuse.

**D. Site-wide macros in `overrides.js`** (works now)

One shared `macros` object for all distill posts — not per-post.

### Recommendation

For a CTMC post, a **per-post `preamble.tex` + Jekyll include + KaTeX bootstrap in `overrides.js`** is the cleanest approach and mirrors how you already handle `bibliography: ctmc.bib` per post.

Example workflow:

```
assets/tex/preambles/ctmc.tex     # \newcommand definitions
_posts/2026-05-10-ctmc.md         # preamble: ctmc.tex
```

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

Yes — for your setup (distill + KaTeX, thin globals + per-post extras), **defining per-post macros in the markdown is the most practical choice**.

### Why it fits

1. **Co-located with content** — CTMC-specific notation (`\lambda`, jump rates, etc.) lives next to the prose that uses it.
2. **No extra infrastructure** — no `preamble.tex`, Jekyll plugin, or build step.
3. **Override is natural** — globals in one place; post-specific defs at the top of that post.
4. **KaTeX supports it** — `\newcommand` / `\gdef` in math can persist through the page if definitions appear **before** the math that uses them.

### Suggested split

| Layer | Where | Example |
|-------|--------|---------|
| **Global (thin)** | `overrides.js` or distill `katex.macros` in layout | `\R`, `\E`, `\Prob` |
| **Per-post** | Top of the `.md` file | `\newcommand{\jumpRate}{\lambda}` |

### Convention for the markdown

Use a short **Notation** block at the top (visible or in a `{% details %}` box):

```markdown
## Notation

$$
\newcommand{\jumpRate}{\lambda}
\newcommand{\stateSpace}{\mathcal{S}}
$$

Rest of post uses $\jumpRate$, $\stateSpace$, …
```

Or hide pure definitions in a details box if you don’t want them in the TOC.

### Caveats

- **KaTeX only** — this applies to distill posts. Regular `layout: post` pages use MathJax; same idea works there with `\newcommand` in math, but it’s a separate config path.
- **Not full LaTeX** — no `\usepackage{...}`; only macro-style definitions.
- **Order matters** — definition block must come before first use.
- **Shared `macros` object** — for `\gdef`/`\newcommand` to persist across the page, global setup should initialize one `macros: {}` in `DMath.katexOptions` (a small `overrides.js` tweak if it isn’t there already).

### vs. `preamble.tex` per post

A `.tex` file per post is better when macros are **large, reused across drafts, or shared with a LaTeX paper**. For thin globals + small per-post overrides, **in-markdown defs are simpler and easier to maintain**.

If you want, I can add the thin global `macros` in `overrides.js` and a Notation template at the top of your CTMC post.

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

**Correct — KaTeX will almost certainly never support `\usepackage{...}`** the way pdfLaTeX/XeLaTeX does.

KaTeX is a **math renderer**, not a TeX engine. It doesn't run `.sty` files or execute TeX macro code. Packages like `amsmath` are written in TeX; KaTeX would need each command reimplemented in JavaScript.

The maintainers have said this directly ([issue #3058](https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX/issues/3058)): full package loading is "impossible or at least a very long way away." There's no roadmap to add it.

### What KaTeX does instead

It **built-in emulates** many common packages — especially `amsmath`, `amssymb`, parts of `mathtools`, `bm`, `color`, etc. See the [Package Emulation wiki](https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX/wiki/Package-Emulation) and [supported functions list](https://katex.org/docs/supported.html).

So this often works without `\usepackage`:

```latex
\begin{align*}
  \E[X] &= \sum_x x \, \Prob(X = x)
\end{align*}
```

But if a command isn't in KaTeX's supported set, `\usepackage` won't help — you'd define it with `\gdef` / `macros` (what we set up for your site).

### If you need real `\usepackage`

| Option | Use when |
|--------|----------|
| **MathJax** (your regular `post` layout) | Broader TeX coverage than KaTeX, still not full LaTeX |
| **Compile with LaTeX → PDF/image** | You need exact paper compatibility |
| **LaTeXML / LaTeX.js** | Full documents, not inline blog math |

### For your distill posts

The practical model is what you have now:

- **Globals** in `overrides.js` (`\R`, `\E`, …)
- **Per-post** hidden `\gdef` block for anything KaTeX doesn't ship with
- **No `\usepackage`** — check [katex.org/docs/supported.html](https://katex.org/docs/supported.html) first; if a command is missing, add a macro

If you hit a specific missing command from a package (e.g. `\argmin` from `statmath`), I can check whether KaTeX already has it or suggest a one-line `\gdef`.

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

**Probably not worth it** for your site — especially for a CTMC post with standard probability notation.

### Why the payoff is small

**MathJax still isn't LaTeX.** It doesn't support `\usepackage{...}` either. You'd gain `tex.macros` in one config file and a few extra TeX packages via MathJax's package loader (`ams`, `boldsymbol`, etc.), but you'd still define custom commands manually — same idea as your hidden `\gdef` block + global macros in `overrides.js`.

**Distill is built around KaTeX.** The template ships with `DMath`, `<d-math>`, and KaTeX auto-render baked into `template.v2.js`. Switching means forking vendored Distill JS, disabling the KaTeX path, and re-wiring typesetting for `d-article`. That's ongoing maintenance, and it diverges from [al-folio upstream](https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio).

**You already load both.** `distill.html` includes MathJax *and* runs KaTeX. Distill math is rendered by KaTeX; MathJax mostly adds weight unless something else triggers it.

### When MathJax might be worth it

| Situation | Verdict |
|-----------|---------|
| CTMC / stochastic posts (`align`, `\mathbb`, `\E`, matrices) | **Stay on KaTeX** — well supported |
| Many unsupported KaTeX commands | Consider MathJax *or* add `\gdef` macros |
| Want one shared `mathjax.html` config everywhere | Nice, but achievable with thin KaTeX globals |
| Need `\usepackage{ tikz }`, custom `.sty`, paper parity | Neither engine — compile LaTeX to PDF/images |

### KaTeX vs MathJax (for your use case)

| | KaTeX (current) | MathJax |
|--|-----------------|---------|
| Speed | Fast | Slower |
| Distill integration | Native | Requires custom fork |
| Macro preamble | `macros` + `\gdef` | `tex.macros` + inline `\newcommand` |
| `\usepackage` | No | No (package loader only for supported bundles) |
| Upstream al-folio | Default | Not default for distill |

### Practical recommendation

**Keep KaTeX for distill.** Your current setup (thin globals in `overrides.js` + hidden per-post `\gdef`) is the right model.

Optional cleanups that help more than a full switch:

1. **Skip MathJax on distill pages** — load it only for `layout: post` to avoid double math stacks.
2. **Expand global KaTeX macros** as notation stabilizes across posts.
3. **Switch a single post to `layout: post`** if it needs heavier math and you want MathJax — only if KaTeX truly blocks you.

If you start hitting specific missing commands (e.g. `\argmin`, a weird arrow, a particular environment), share them — often a one-line `\gdef` is enough and cheaper than migrating the whole distill stack.

Two bugs were breaking macros (and much of the math rendering):

1. **The `DMath` patch was too aggressive** — replacing `katexOptions` with `defineProperty` interfered with Distill’s static setter and could prevent KaTeX from starting.
2. **Delimiter mismatch** — Kramdown turns `$$...$$` into `\[\...\]`, but distill only registered `$` / `$$`, so display math stayed as raw text.

### Fixes

**`overrides.js`** — rewritten to:
- Use one shared `window.__distillKatexMacros` object (required for `\gdef` to persist)
- Process `.katex-preamble` with `katex.renderToString` before the rest of the page renders
- Patch `addKatex`, `katexLoadedCallback`, and `renderContent` (no `defineProperty` hack)

**`distill.html`** — added `\[` `\]` and `\(` `\)` delimiters for Kramdown’s LaTeX-style output.

**`ctmc.md`** — changed `\Prob()` to `\Prob(X = k)` so the example is valid math.

Global macros: `\R`, `\N`, `\E`, `\Prob`. Per-post defs stay in the hidden `.katex-preamble` div at the top of the markdown.

        <p>In this post, we will go over the basics of continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs).
The main goal is to provide an intuitive view of CTMCs.</p>

<details><summary>Prerequisites</summary>
<p>This post assumes a basic understanding of:</p>

<ul>
  <li>probability (random variables, expectation, conditional probability)</li>
  <li>calculus (limits, derivatives, integrals)</li>
  <li>discrete-time Markov chains (transition matrices, stationary distributions)</li>
</ul>
</details>

<h2 id="poisson-processes">Poisson Processes</h2>
<p>Poisson processes are the simplest form of CTMCs, and provide the intuition we need for the general case.</p>

<p>First, let’s consider the binomial distribution, i.e., the probability of getting $k$ heads in $n$ coin flips.</p>

\[\Prob(X = k)\]

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

Yes — we were overcomplicating it.

### Recommended way (upstream + KaTeX docs)

**Upstream Distill / al-folio:** put everything in the `katex` JSON in the distill front matter. Distill passes that object straight into `katex.render` / auto-render. No JS patching.

**KaTeX docs:** define macros as a JS object:

```js
macros: { "\\Prob": "\\mathbb{P}" }
```

That’s it. Hidden `.katex-preamble` divs, `\gdef`, and DMath monkey-patches are not the Distill path.

### What I changed

1. **Removed** all KaTeX patching from `overrides.js` (back to footnote/citation styles only).
2. **Put macros in** `_layouts/distill.html`’s `katex` block (the Distill-native place).
3. **Kept** `\[` `\]` delimiters — kramdown turns your `$$...$$` into `\[...\]`, so Distill must recognize those.
4. **Removed** the hidden preamble from the CTMC post.

Hard refresh. `\Prob(X = k)` should render as blackboard **P**.

### Per-post macros later

Simplest options that match this model:

| Approach | Complexity |
|----------|------------|
| Site-wide macros in `distill.html` (current) | Low — fine for `\R`, `\E`, `\Prob` |
| Per-post `katex.macros` in YAML front matter, merged in the layout | Medium — clean if you need it |
| Hidden `\gdef` blocks | High — needs shared `macros` object wiring Distill doesn’t do by default |

For now, add CTMC-specific macros to the layout `macros` object when you need them. We can wire per-post YAML macros later if the global set gets too large.
